newsitem.title: CHINA: China ends trial of six for Xinjiang riot.
newsitem.headline: China ends trial of six for Xinjiang riot.

text.p: China has ended hearings for six men on trial for their role in rioting in the Moslem region of Xinjiang last month, a court official said on Friday.
The official, speaking by telephone from China's far northwestern city of Yining where anti-Chinese riots erupted last month, said the verdict would be announced in April.
The six men, all members of the ethnic Uighur minority, have been charged with hooliganism and endangering social order. They could face the death sentence if convicted.
Officials have not identified the men, saying only they were in their 30s and jobless.
Xinjiang, a vast region that is home to many Turkic-speaking people like the Uighurs, has had a long history of ethnic friction and has been rocked by Moslem separatist violence of late.
Militants say they want to set up their own state of "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang.
The Yining riot began as a demonstration for Xinjiang independence and turned violent, leaving nine people dead and 198 injured.
Xinjiang's capital of Urumqi was rocked by a series of bus bombs last month in attacks that killed nine and wounded 74.
Exiled ethnic Uighurs have claimed responsibility for the bombings and vowed to stage more attacks until they gain complete freedom for their homeland.

Officials have denied statements by exiles in Almaty, capital of neighbouring Kazakhstan, that China had planned to execute two religious students from the Uighur minority on Thursday for the Yining riots.
A small group of Uighur exiles staged a noisy protest outside the Chinese embassy in Almaty on Thursday, shouting separatist slogans.
